Juanes closes out his North American tour in San Diego. The Grammy-winning Colombian rock star plays Gallagher Square at Petco Park on Thursday, October 22, 2026 — the last of 28 dates on a run that started in Orlando in early September. He’s touring behind JuanesTeban, his new concept album, with a brand-new stage production built around it. Tour finales tend to be the loosest, longest nights of a run, and San Diego gets this one.

Quick Info

  • Date: Thursday, October 22, 2026
  • Show: 8:00 PM
  • Venue: Gallagher Square at Petco Park
  • Support: Andrea Bejar
  • Tickets: General admission from $68.70
  • Parking: Reserve now
  • Why it matters: Final night of the North American tour

Tickets are on sale now. It’s a general admission lawn show, so a later arrival just means a spot farther back — but on a tour-closing Thursday with a big local Latin music crowd, don’t count on a walk-up.

About Juanes

Juan Esteban Aristizábal Vásquez — Juanes — grew up in Colombia’s Antioquia region and started out as the frontman and guitarist for the Medellín metal band Ekhymosis. He went solo in 2000, and two years later Un Día Normal made him the biggest name in Latin rock. That album sat in the top 10 of Billboard’s Latin chart for a record 92 weeks and won six Latin Grammys on its own.

The hits kept coming: “A Dios le Pido,” “Es Por Ti,” “Fotografía” with Nelly Furtado, and “La Camisa Negra,” which charted all over Europe without a word of English. He’s still winning, too — Vida Cotidiana took the Grammy for Best Latin Rock or Alternative Album in 2024.

Juanes has never kept politics out of the music. In 2008 he organized the first Paz Sin Fronteras concert on a border bridge between Colombia and Venezuela, then took the idea to Havana’s Plaza de la Revolución the next year. Time named him one of its 100 Most Influential People.

The New Album: JuanesTeban

JuanesTeban came out March 6 on Universal. The title mashes up his stage name and his birth name, and the whole 16-track record is built around that split — light and dark, the rock star and the guy from Antioquia. He co-produced it with Argentine producer Nico Cotton and pulled in a strong guest list: Bomba Estéreo, Mon Laferte, Vivir Quintana, Rawayana and Conociendo Rusia. Musically it bounces between rock, cumbia and the Colombian folk sounds he’s always come back to.

Songs to know before the show: “Hagamos Que,” “Una Noche Contigo,” and “El Gran Día.”

What to Expect

Expect the new material up front and the classics where they belong. A Juanes set leans hard on his guitar playing, he talks to the crowd about where the songs came from, and nobody leaves without hearing “La Camisa Negra” and “A Dios le Pido.” The 2026 tour also carries a new production designed around JuanesTeban, so this isn’t a stripped-down club show.

Watch Juanes perform “A Dios le Pido” live

Tour Finale: Last nights of a tour are when the band is at its tightest and most relaxed at the same time. That’s when you get the extra encore, the deep cut, or a guest walking out from side stage. No promises — but if you were picking one night of this tour to see, this is the one.

Gallagher Square at Petco Park

Gallagher Square is the 2.8-acre lawn beyond the outfield at Petco Park. You can stand down front near the stage or hang back on the grass slope with the ballpark lit up behind you. For an artist who usually plays arenas, it’s a much closer look.

First-timer? Read the complete guide to Gallagher Square concerts.

Enter through the Balboa Gate on J Street.
Address: 100 Park Blvd, San Diego, CA 92101

Public Transportation (Recommended)

The MTS Trolley is your best option on a weeknight. All three lines serve Petco Park:

  • Green Line: From Old Town, Mission Valley, SDSU
  • Blue Line: From South Bay
  • Orange Line: From East County

Get off at 12th & Imperial Station, a short walk to the gate.

Park & Ride: Drive to Old Town Transit Center, park for free, and ride the trolley downtown. Perfect for North County.

Rideshare

Check our rideshare guide for Uber/Lyft pickup and drop-off locations.

What to Bring

Review the Petco Park bag policy before you arrive. Only small clutches (4.5” × 6.5”) and clear bags are allowed.

  • Valid ID (required for entry and alcohol purchase, 21+)
  • Mobile ticket on your phone
  • Credit/debit card (most vendors are cashless)
  • Light jacket — late October nights downtown get cool once the sun’s gone
  • Comfortable shoes for standing and dancing
